title: Badge
summary: A short word next to what it describes, the system's tag: a mono label on a tint of its color for a status or a category, or in an edge for a plain list.
use: A status next to what it describes, such as paid, pending or cancelled in a table's cell.
A category or a name in a list of them, such as the technologies of a project: the tag, or the outlined tag where a list of tints would be loud.
notFor: An action: that is a button, which a badge never looks like.
A count or a dot on an icon or an avatar.
A message about the page: that is a callout, or a status line.

parts.root: The box: the tint or the edge, and the room around the word.
parts.label: The word.
parts.leading-icon: An icon before the word, which repeats what it says, such as a check before paid.

variants.primary: The tag, on a tint of the interactive color: a category or a label, such as new or a technology. `.ws-tag` is this kind at md.
variants.success: A status that went well: paid.
variants.warning: A status that needs attention soon: expiring.
variants.danger: A status that failed or ended: cancelled.
variants.neutral: A plain fact without a status: draft.
variants.outline: The outlined tag, in the text color, for a plain list where tints would be loud, such as a project's stack. `.ws-tag--outline` is this kind at md.

sizes.xs: A dense row, next to a caption.
sizes.sm: Next to a small control, or in a bar.
sizes.md: Every other badge: in text, in a table's cell, in a card's header. The size of `.ws-tag`.
sizes.lg: Next to a large control or a minor heading.
sizes.xl: Next to the title of a landing page.

states.rest: Always: a badge is not interactive, so it has no other state.

rules: A badge is text, a `span` with no role, and assistive technology reads its word where it stands. A status badge always has its word: its color only repeats it.
An icon in it repeats the word, so it is hidden from assistive technology.
It takes no focus. A badge that does something is a button, and a badge that goes somewhere is a link.

forcedColors: A tint is a background, which forced colors take away: a badge on a tint keeps its word, in the system's text color, and the word carries it alone, as it does in every theme. An implementation may draw an edge there, in `CanvasText`, as ui-vue does.
The outlined badge's edge is a real border, which forced colors keep.

An icon takes the system's text color. An icon drawn as an SVG in `currentcolor` does so by itself; an icon drawn as a mask needs its background set in forced colors, where every background is the page's.
motion: Nothing moves: a badge has no state to change into.
content: One or two words, without a period: paid, pending, new.
Lower case as in a terminal, except a name, which keeps its own: TypeScript, Lisbon.
A status badge says its status in its word, in every color: never a color alone, and never a color that says something else than its word.
notes: The kinds are those in use: the soft variant in each color, and the outlined neutral one. Nuxt UI's solid and subtle variants, and the outline in another color, are left out.

The outlined badge's edge is `color.border`, as a card's is, which reads at less than 3:1 on the page. It frames a word that carries the badge alone, as a card's edge frames its content, so the spec names the role and the tier has no edge for a tag: an edge of the tier has to reach 3:1.

The outlined badge's edge is inside its `padding-block` and outside its `padding-inline`, as `.ws-tag--outline` draws it: at md it is 4 px taller and 6 px wider than a badge on a tint. Its `padding-block` is the token less the edge's width.
An xs badge has no `padding-block`: its line is its height, 18 px.

Its icons are `size.icon`, 16 px, at every size, the icon of the system's text: the 12 px and 14 px icons of ui-vue's smaller badges are off its scale, and a badge does not grow its icon as a control does.
`.ws-tag` and `.ws-tag--outline` read the tag group, and a browser test holds them to the primary and the outline kinds at md, so the system's own tag and every implementation's badge stay alike.

ui-vue.library: Nuxt UI 4.12, themed by ui-vue's app config
ui-vue.today: The soft variant is its default, in every color a tint under the color's text, and at md the primary one is `.ws-tag`: the small radius, the label in mono at its regular weight, 2 px by 8 px. Its paddings, gaps and text styles match the spec at every size. In forced colors every badge draws an edge in `CanvasText`.

deviations.summary: The outlined badge's edge is an inset ring, a box shadow, and a border only in forced colors, and it keeps the padding of a badge on a tint, so at md it is 4 px shorter and 6 px narrower than `.ws-tag--outline`. So the outline's rows for `border-color`, `border-style`, `border-width`, `padding-inline` and `padding-block` do not hold.
Its icons are 12 px at xs and sm and 14 px at md, where the spec takes `size.icon`, 16 px, at every size.

It reads the roles and measures by their Tailwind utilities, such as `bg-tag-bg` and `px-2`, not the component tokens, such as `bg-(--ws-tag-primary-bg)` and `px-(--ws-tag-padding-inline-md)`, so a change of the tier does not reach it.
Its gallery marks no example with `data-spec`, and shows the sizes in the primary color only, so the outlined badge's sizes are missing.

beyond: The solid and subtle variants, such as the subtle success badge, in stock, of its example of a part held in the other theme.
The outlined badge in a color other than neutral, its edge in that color.
A square badge of an icon alone, and a badge with an avatar.
